questions.q: What was the coracle's worst habit?
choices: It kept turning round and round instead of going straight
It was too heavy to carry
It tipped over in small waves
questions.evidence: turning round and round was the manoeuvre she was best at

questions.q: How did Jim manage to reach the ship even though he could not steer the coracle well?
choices: The tide carried him down to it
A pirate threw him a rope
questions.evidence: I never should have made the ship at all but for the tide

questions.q: Why did Jim stop before cutting the tight hawser (anchor rope)?
choices: He realized a taut rope suddenly cut could knock him out of the water
He changed his mind about the plan
questions.evidence: a taut hawser, suddenly cut, is a thing as dangerous as a kicking horse

questions.q: What did Jim do once a puff of wind made the hawser go slack?
choices: He cut the strands one after another until only two were left
He climbed up the hawser onto the deck
He cut the whole rope at once
He tied the coracle to the ship
questions.evidence: cut one strand after another, till the vessel swung only by two

questions.q: Who were the two men on board the HISPANIOLA?
choices: Israel Hands and the man in the red night-cap
questions.evidence: The other was, of course, my friend of the red night-cap

questions.q: What were the two men in the cabin doing?
questions.evidence: they were not only tipsy; it was plain that they were furiously angry

questions.q: Jim says the buccaneers "were as callous as the sea they sailed on." "Callous" means:
questions.evidence: all these buccaneers were as callous as the sea they sailed on

questions.q: After cutting the last fibres of the hawser, what did Jim grab as he pushed away from the ship?
choices: A light cord trailing over the stern
questions.evidence: my hands came across a light cord that was trailing overboard

questions.q: What did Jim see when he looked through the cabin window?
choices: Hands and his companion locked in a deadly wrestle
questions.evidence: Hands and his companion locked together in deadly wrestle

questions.q: Why was Jim's heart jumping when he saw the camp-fire behind him?
choices: The current had turned and was sweeping the ship and coracle out toward the open sea
The fire had spread to the woods
He thought the stockade was burning
questions.evidence: it went spinning through the narrows for the open sea

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Jim cuts the HISPANIOLA loose, and both the ship and his tiny boat are swept out to sea
Jim captures the ship from the pirates
Jim returns safely to the stockade
Hands discovers Jim and takes him prisoner
questions.evidence: with a good, tough effort, cut the last fibres through
